previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with lethargy and hypotension, suspected to be due to a urinary tract infection, given her history of recurrent UTIs with resistant organisms. She was initially managed in the ICU with IV fluids and broad-spectrum antibiotics. Her course was complicated by a transient fever and hypotension requiring readmission to the ICU, but she remained stable overall. Imaging showed progressive bibasilar consolidation concerning for pneumonia or cardiac congestion, though her respiratory status improved. A yeast infection was identified in the urine, and she developed a groin rash treated with topical antifungal. She completed a course of IV antibiotics and was transitioned to oral amoxicillin. Her mental status normalized, and she was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to complete her antibiotic course, manage the rash, and follow up with her primary doctor.
problems: Urinary tract infection, site not specified

Brief Hospital Course:
___ yo female w/ T1-2 paraplegia ___ MVA, chronic bladder atony, 
and recurrent multi-drug resistent UTIs who presents to the ED 
with increased lethargy after recent admission for urosepsis.

persistent UTI not responding to amoxicillin. Although

when initially switched to amoxicillin. Of note, pt afebrile 
with nl WBC. Pt started empirically on vanc and ceftriaxone in 
ED. UA unremarkable with urine culture negative (collected prior 
to IV antibiotics administration). Blood cultures, also drawn 
prior to IV antibiotics, are pending to date. Of note, question 
of RLL PNA v. atelectasis on CXR (h/o of MRSA PNA), although CXR 
appears improved from prior taken during last admission. Pt 
noted to have cough productive of some sputum, respiratory 
culture still pending on discharge. She remained afebrile with 
no left shift on ___. As infectious work-up negative to date and 
pt with nl electrolytes, most likely etiology of lethargy is 
dehydration ___ decreased po intake. There was evidence of 
hemoconcentration on admission labs although Cr at baseline. Pt 
did seem more alert to her to her PCA ___ after receiving IVF 
overnight. Pt switched back to po amoxicillin, on which she was 
discharged, to follow up with Dr. ___ on ___.

# Relative hypotension: SBP noted to be ___ at home and in ED, 
responded appropriately to fluid hydration, suggesting at least 
some component of volume depletion. Although creatinine was at 
baseline, evidence of hemoconcentration as above. Concern for 
early sign of sepsis, but patient remained hemodynamically 
stable. Pt kept on IV fluids overnight. On discharge, patient 
advised to stay well-hydrated and increase salt intake.

# Depression: Pt appeared frustrated to be back in the hospital 
but had good support of her friend and care assistant. Continued 
on home citalopram and clonazepam.

# Recurrent UTIs: Pt may need to see Urology as outpatient to 
evaluate catheterization method as pt has had multiple

radiology_notes.text:
AP PORTABLE CHEST, ___ AT 15:48 HOURS

HISTORY:  Hypoxia and lethargy.

COMPARISON:  Multiple priors, the most recent dated ___.

FINDINGS:  Since the prior examination, the right internal jugular central
line and left upper extremity PICC line have been removed.  No support tubes
and lines are appreciated.  There is extensive hardware in the included
bilateral humeri as well as extensive rib cage deformity similar to the prior
exam.  Volume status has been improved with no frank interstitial edema noted.
Subtle atelectasis is noted in the right perihilar region.  The cardiac
silhouette size is also decreased but still remains overall enlarged
consistent with longstanding cardiomegaly.  No definite effusion or
pneumothorax is seen.  There is questionable density in the right lung base
and poor definition of the right hemidiaphragm.

IMPRESSION:  RIght basilar denisty.  This may reflect atelectasis; however, an
early developing pneumonia is difficult to exclude.  Conversely, there may be
an influence of soft tissue attenuation.  If clinical suspicion remains high,
consider PA and lateral views in the radiology suite for more sensitive
evaluation.
